questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If tan θ = 20/21, where θ is an acute angle, what is the value of (29 sin θ + 29 cos θ) / (29 cos θ - 20)?
questions.solution:
Given tan θ = Opposite / Adjacent = 20/21.
By Pythagorean triplet (20, 21, 29):
Hypotenuse = sqrt(20² + 21²) = sqrt(400 + 441) = sqrt(841) = 29.
Then sin θ = 20/29 and cos θ = 21/29.
Substituting these values:
Numerator = 29 * (20/29) + 29 * (21/29) = 20 + 21 = 41.
Denominator = 29 * (21/29) - 20 = 21 - 20 = 1.
Result = 41 / 1 = 41.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet: Triplet is (20, 21, 29). Directly: 29 sin θ = 20, 29 cos θ = 21. Expression = (20 + 21) / (21 - 20) = 41.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If cosec θ = 17/8 for an acute angle θ, what is the value of (17 cos θ + 15 tan θ) / (17 sin θ)?
questions.solution:
Given cosec θ = 17/8, so sin θ = 8/17.
Using the Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17):
Opposite = 8, Hypotenuse = 17, Adjacent = sqrt(17² - 8²) = 15.
Thus, cos θ = 15/17 and tan θ = 8/15.
Numerator = 17 * (15/17) + 15 * (8/15) = 15 + 8 = 23.
Denominator = 17 * (8/17) = 8.
Value = 23/8.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet: Triplet (8, 15, 17) gives 17 cos θ = 15, 15 tan θ = 8, 17 sin θ = 8. Expression = (15 + 8) / 8 = 23/8.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The side of a square is increased by 4 cm. As a result, its area increases by 128 cm². What was the original side length of the square?
questions.solution:
Let the original side length of the square be x cm.
Original Area = x² cm².
New side length = (x + 4) cm.
New Area = (x + 4)² = x² + 8x + 16 cm².
Given: New Area - Original Area = 128
(x² + 8x + 16) - x² = 128
8x + 16 = 128
8x = 112
x = 14 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Delta: (Area Difference - Δ²) / (2 * Δ) = (128 - 16) / 8 = 112 / 8 = 14 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The length of a rectangle is 6 cm more than its breadth. If the length is increased by 3 cm and the breadth is decreased by 2 cm, the area remains unchanged. What is the original area of the rectangle?
questions.solution:
Let breadth = b cm. Then length = (b + 6) cm.
Original Area = b(b + 6) = b² + 6b cm².
New length = (b + 6 + 3) = (b + 9) cm.
New breadth = (b - 2) cm.
New Area = (b + 9)(b - 2) = b² + 7b - 18 cm².
Since areas are equal:
b² + 6b = b² + 7b - 18
b = 18 cm.
Length = 18 + 6 = 24 cm.
Original Area = 24 * 18 = 432 cm².
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Equation: Setting areas equal: b² + 6b = (b + 9)(b - 2) = b² + 7b - 18 => b = 18. Area = 24 * 18 = 432 cm².

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A right pyramid has a square base of side 16 cm. If the height of the pyramid is 15 cm, find its total surface area (in cm²).
questions.solution:
Base side a = 16 cm.
Distance from center of base to any side = a / 2 = 16 / 2 = 8 cm.
Height h = 15 cm.
Slant height l = sqrt(h² + (a/2)²) = sqrt(15² + 8²) = sqrt(225 + 64) = sqrt(289) = 17 cm (Pythagorean triplet 8-15-17).
Base Area = a² = 16² = 256 cm².
Lateral Surface Area = (1/2) * Perimeter * l = (1/2) * (4 * 16) * 17 = 32 * 17 = 544 cm².
Total Surface Area = Base Area + LSA = 256 + 544 = 800 cm².
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet: Half-side = 8, h = 15 => slant height l = 17. TSA = a² + 2*a*l = 256 + 2(16)(17) = 256 + 544 = 800 cm².

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A right pyramid stands on a square base of side 12 cm. If its slant height is 10 cm, what is the volume of the pyramid (in cm³)?
questions.solution:
Base side a = 12 cm.
Distance from center of base to any edge = a / 2 = 6 cm.
Slant height l = 10 cm.
Vertical height h = sqrt(l² - (a/2)²) = sqrt(10² - 6²) = sqrt(100 - 36) = sqrt(64) = 8 cm (triplet 6-8-10).
Base Area = 12 * 12 = 144 cm².
Volume = (1/3) * Base Area * Height = (1/3) * 144 * 8 = 48 * 8 = 384 cm³.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A chord of length 30 cm is drawn in a circle of radius 17 cm. What is the perpendicular distance of the chord from the centre of the circle?
questions.solution:
The perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord.
Half-length of chord = 30 / 2 = 15 cm.
Radius r = 17 cm.
Distance from centre d = sqrt(r² - 15²) = sqrt(17² - 15²) = sqrt(289 - 225) = sqrt(64) = 8 cm.
This corresponds to the Pythagorean triplet (8, 15, 17).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet: Radius = 17, half-chord = 15 => Distance = 8 cm by (8, 15, 17) triplet.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A vertical pole of height 24 m casts a shadow of length 8*sqrt(3) m on the ground. What is the angle of elevation of the sun?
questions.solution:
Let θ be the angle of elevation of the sun.
tan θ = Height of pole / Length of shadow
tan θ = 24 / (8*sqrt(3)) = 3 / sqrt(3) = sqrt(3).
Since tan 60° = sqrt(3), θ = 60°.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Ratio: tan θ = 24 / (8√3) = √3 => θ = 60° directly.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: In triangle ABC, a line DE is drawn parallel to BC intersecting AB at D and AC at E such that AD : DB = 3 : 2. What is the ratio of the area of triangle ADE to the area of trapezium BDEC?
questions.solution:
Given AD : DB = 3 : 2.
Then AB = AD + DB = 3 + 2 = 5 units.
So AD / AB = 3 / 5.
Since DE || BC, triangle ADE is similar to triangle ABC.
Area(ADE) / Area(ABC) = (AD / AB)² = (3 / 5)² = 9 / 25.
Area of trapezium BDEC = Area(ABC) - Area(ADE) = 25 - 9 = 16 units.
Ratio Area(ADE) : Area(BDEC) = 9 : 16.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Area Ratio: Ratio of sides is 3 : 5. Area ADE = 3² = 9, Total = 5² = 25. Trapezium = 25 - 9 = 16. Ratio = 9 : 16.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: What is the slope of the line passing through the points P(3, -2) and Q(-1, 6)?
questions.solution:
The slope m of a line passing through points (x1, y1) and (x2, y2) is given by:
m = (y2 - y1) / (x2 - x1)
Here (x1, y1) = (3, -2) and (x2, y2) = (-1, 6).
m = (6 - (-2)) / (-1 - 3) = (6 + 2) / (-4) = 8 / (-4) = -2.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If k > 0 and the matrix A = [[k + 4, 3], [12, k - 1]] is singular, what is the value of k?
questions.solution:
A matrix is singular if its determinant is equal to zero.
det(A) = (k + 4)(k - 1) - (3)(12) = 0
k² + 3k - 4 - 36 = 0
k² + 3k - 40 = 0
(k + 8)(k - 5) = 0
Since k > 0, k = 5.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Determinant: (k + 4)(k - 1) = 36. Test options: For k = 5, 9 * 4 = 36. Correct immediately.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: What is the value of: 1/(sqrt(2) + 1) + 1/(sqrt(3) + sqrt(2)) + 1/(sqrt(4) + sqrt(3)) + ... + 1/(sqrt(100) + sqrt(99))?
questions.solution:
Rationalising each term by multiplying numerator and denominator by its conjugate:
1 / (sqrt(n+1) + sqrt(n)) = sqrt(n+1) - sqrt(n).
Sum = (sqrt(2) - 1) + (sqrt(3) - sqrt(2)) + (sqrt(4) - sqrt(3)) + ... + (sqrt(100) - sqrt(99)).
All intermediate terms cancel out in a telescoping ladder:
Sum = sqrt(100) - 1 = 10 - 1 = 9.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Telescoping: Telescoping series gives sqrt(last) - sqrt(first) = sqrt(100) - sqrt(1) = 10 - 1 = 9.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If x ∈ {-4, -1, 2, 5} and y ∈ {-3, 0, 4}, what is the maximum possible value of (x² - 2xy + y²)?
questions.solution:
Notice that x² - 2xy + y² = (x - y)².
To maximize (x - y)², we need to maximize the absolute difference |x - y|.
Possible values for x - y:
If x = 5 and y = -3: x - y = 5 - (-3) = 8, so (x - y)² = 64.
If x = -4 and y = 4: x - y = -4 - 4 = -8, so (x - y)² = 64.
No other pair yields a larger difference.
Therefore, the maximum value is 64.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Identity: Expression is (x - y)². Max difference is 5 - (-3) = 8 (or -4 - 4 = -8). Max value = 8² = 64.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If the 8-digit number 785x367y is completely divisible by 72, what is the value of (x + y)?
questions.solution:
For a number to be divisible by 72, it must be divisible by both 8 and 9.
Divisibility by 8 requires the last three digits '67y' to be divisible by 8.
670 / 8 = 83 remainder 6, so 672 / 8 = 84. Thus, y = 2.
Divisibility by 9 requires the sum of digits to be a multiple of 9:
Sum = 7 + 8 + 5 + x + 3 + 6 + 7 + 2 = 38 + x.
The nearest multiple of 9 greater than 38 is 45.
38 + x = 45 => x = 7.
Therefore, (x + y) = 7 + 2 = 9.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Divisibility: 67y div by 8 => y = 2. Sum = 38 + x div by 9 => x = 7. x + y = 7 + 2 = 9.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A number is first increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. The number so obtained is 50 less than the original number. What was the original number?
questions.solution:
Let the original number be N.
Net percentage change after +20% and -20% = 20 - 20 - (20 * 20 / 100) = -4% (a decrease of 4%).
Given: 4% of N = 50
(4 / 100) * N = 50
N = (50 * 100) / 4 = 50 * 25 = 1,250.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A dishonest dealer claims to sell sugar at cost price, but he uses a false weight of 920 grams instead of 1 kilogram. What is his profit percentage (rounded to two decimal places)?
questions.solution:
The dealer provides 920 g of sugar but charges the cost price of 1000 g.
Cost Price to dealer = cost of 920 g.
Selling Price obtained = cost of 1000 g.
Profit = 1000 - 920 = 80 g.
Profit Percentage = (Error / Actual Weight Given) * 100 = (80 / 920) * 100
= (2 / 23) * 100 = 200 / 23 ≈ 8.6956% ≈ 8.70%.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Dealer Formula: Profit % = [Error / (Actual Weight Given)] * 100 = (80 / 920) * 100 = 200 / 23 ≈ 8.70%.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain sum of money at 8% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 96. What is the sum?
questions.solution:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI is given by:
Difference = P * (R / 100)²
96 = P * (8 / 100)²
96 = P * (64 / 10000)
P = (96 * 10000) / 64 = 1.5 * 10000 = Rs. 15,000.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 18 days, while B can complete the same work in 27 days. They work together for 6 days, and then A leaves. How many days will B alone take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
Total work = LCM(18, 27) = 54 units.
A's efficiency = 54 / 18 = 3 units/day.
B's efficiency = 54 / 27 = 2 units/day.
Combined efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day.
Work done in 6 days together = 6 * 5 = 30 units.
Remaining work = 54 - 30 = 24 units.
Time taken by B alone = Remaining work / B's efficiency = 24 / 2 = 12 days.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec LCM: Work = 54 u. Rates: A=3, B=2. Work in 6 days = 6 * 5 = 30 u. Left = 24 u. B takes 24 / 2 = 12 days.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A train 180 metres long is running at a uniform speed of 54 km/h. How many seconds will it take to pass completely over a platform 120 metres long?
questions.solution:
Total distance to be covered = Length of train + Length of platform = 180 + 120 = 300 metres.
Speed of train in m/s = 54 * (5 / 18) = 3 * 5 = 15 m/s.
Time taken = Total Distance / Speed = 300 / 15 = 20 seconds.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Conversion: 54 km/h = 15 m/s. Total distance = 180 + 120 = 300 m. Time = 300 / 15 = 20 s.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A boat can travel 36 km downstream in 2 hours and 24 km upstream in 3 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
questions.solution:
Downstream speed u = Distance / Time = 36 / 2 = 18 km/h.
Upstream speed v = Distance / Time = 24 / 3 = 8 km/h.
Speed of the boat in still water = (u + v) / 2 = (18 + 8) / 2 = 26 / 2 = 13 km/h.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A vessel contains 60 litres of a mixture of milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2. How much water must be added to this mixture so that the ratio of milk to water becomes 1 : 1?
questions.solution:
Total quantity = 60 litres.
Milk = 60 * (3/5) = 36 litres.
Water = 60 * (2/5) = 24 litres.
Let x litres of water be added to make the ratio 1 : 1.
Milk / Water = 36 / (24 + x) = 1 / 1
24 + x = 36
x = 12 litres.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Ratio: Milk remains 36 L. For 1:1, water must also be 36 L. Added water = 36 - 24 = 12 L.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of a father and his son is 7 : 2. After 10 years, the ratio of their ages will become 9 : 4. What is the present age of the father?
questions.solution:
Let the present ages of father and son be 7x and 2x years.
After 10 years:
(7x + 10) / (2x + 10) = 9 / 4
Cross-multiplying:
4(7x + 10) = 9(2x + 10)
28x + 40 = 18x + 90
10x = 50 => x = 5.
Father's present age = 7x = 7 * 5 = 35 years.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Age Hook: Vertical difference: 9 - 7 = 2 units, 4 - 2 = 2 units. 2 units = 10 years => 1 unit = 5 years. Father = 7 * 5 = 35 years.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Referring to the bookstore data in Q.23, what is the percentage increase in books sold by store P from January to March?
questions.solution:
Books sold by P in January = 180.
Books sold by P in March = 250.
Increase = 250 - 180 = 70.

questions.question: Referring to the bookstore data in Q.23, what is the ratio of books sold by store Q in January to books sold by store S in March?
