Step 2: The text advocates transitioning to 'community-anchored stewardship' and states that 'Integrating indigenous ecological knowledge with statutory wildlife protection corridors and payment for ecosystem services (PES) represents the most viable blueprint...'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Concluding sentence: 'Community stewardship + indigenous knowledge + wildlife corridors + PES'.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks:

The wildlife crime intelligence unit worked undercover to ________ actionable intelligence regarding the ________ smuggling of tiger pelts.
questions.solution:
1. Elicit (verb) means to evoke, draw out, or extract (a response, answer, or information) from someone. Blank 1 requires elicit.
2. Illicit (adjective) means forbidden by law, rules, or custom; illegal. Blank 2 requires illicit ('illicit smuggling').
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Elicit = Extract information (verb); Illicit = Illegal act (adjective).

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank:

Monetary economists warned that the domestic currency would rapidly ________ against global benchmark currencies if foreign portfolio outflows accelerated.
questions.solution:
Depreciate means to diminish in value or purchasing power over time (particularly currency, assets, or equipment).
Deprecate means to express earnest disapproval of, disparage, or belittle (e.g., self-deprecating remarks).
A currency falling in market value requires depreciate.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Depreciate = Decrease in financial value. Deprecate = Disapprove / criticize.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank:

The legislative ethics committee voted overwhelmingly to officially ________ the member for his unparliamentary behaviour during the session.
questions.solution:
Censure means to express severe disapproval of someone or their actions, typically in a formal statement or reprimand.
Censor means an official who examines books, films, or news and suppresses unacceptable parts, or the act of suppressing them.
Sensor is a technical device that detects or measures physical properties.
Officially rebuking a lawmaker requires censure.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Censure = Formal condemnation / severe reprimand. Censor = Cut out objectionable media.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the given word: FASTIDIOUS
questions.solution:
Fastidious means very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail; hard to please; meticulous.
Meticulous means showing great attention to detail; very careful and precise (exact synonym).
Careless, Slapdash, and Indifferent describe sloppy or unconcerned behavior.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Fastidious = Hard to please / Detail-obsessed -> Meticulous.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the most appropriate SYNONYM of the given word: SPURIOUS
questions.solution:
Spurious means not being what it purports to be; false, forged, fake, or invalid.
Counterfeit means made in exact imitation of something valuable with the intention to deceive; forged or bogus (exact synonym).
Authentic, Genuine, and Legitimate are direct antonyms.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Spurious = Fake / Bogus / Fraudulent -> Counterfeit.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word: NADIR
questions.solution:
Nadir means the lowest point in the fortunes of a person or organization; rock bottom.
Zenith means the highest point reached by a celestial body, or the peak/culmination of success (exact antonym).
Abyss, Bottom, and Depths are synonyms of nadir.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Nadir = Lowest rock bottom <-> Zenith = Highest peak / pinnacle.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word: TREACHERY
questions.solution:
Treachery means betrayal of trust; deceptive action or treason.
Fidelity means faithfulness to a person, cause, or belief, demonstrated by continuing loyalty and support (exact antonym).
Betrayal, Perjury, and Perfidy are synonyms of treachery.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Treachery = Betrayal / Treason <-> Fidelity = Faithfulness / Loyalty.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words: A person who collects, preserves, and possesses a passionate love for books
questions.solution:
A bibliophile (root biblio- = book + -phile = lover) is a person who collects or has a great love of books.
A philatelist collects postage stamps.
A numismatist collects coins and medals.
A bibliographer compiles lists of books and publications.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Biblio- (book) + phile (lover) -> Bibliophile = Book lover.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words: The sweet sugary fluid secreted by plants and flowers to attract pollinators, or a delicious divine drink
questions.solution:
Nectar is the sugary fluid produced by flowering plants to attract pollinating insects and birds, and in classical mythology, the drink of the gods.
Ambrosia is the food of the gods.
Elixir is a magical or medicinal potion.
Concoction is a mixture of various ingredients.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Nectar = Sweet floral fluid secreted for pollinators (drink of gods).

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence:

Dwelling endlessly upon our lost corporate sponsorship is simply <u>crying over spilled milk</u>; we must strategize for the next funding round.
options: Accidentally dropping dairy containers in a retail supermarket
Demanding immediate full financial restitution for a breach of contract
Celebrating an unexpected and dramatic reversal of commercial fortune
Wasting time mourning or lamenting over past losses that cannot be undone
questions.solution: The idiom 'cry over spilled milk' means to waste time feeling upset, angry, or sorrowful about a misfortune, mistake, or loss that has already happened and cannot be reversed.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Cry over spilled milk = Regretting what can never be undone.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the given sentence:

Before the organizers could officially announce the celebrity guest, a technician carelessly <u>spilled the beans</u> on social media.
options: Demanded an exorbitant payment for audiovisual services
Refused to collaborate with the marketing department
Scattered agricultural produce across the event venue
Inadvertently or prematurely revealed confidential information or a secret
questions.solution: The idiom 'spill the beans' means to divulge a secret prematurely, indiscreetly, or inadvertently.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Spill the beans = Let the cat out of the bag / Reveal a secret.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given options:
questions.solution:
The misspelled word is 'Priviledge'. The correct spelling is Privilege (P-R-I-V-I-L-E-G-E; there is NO 'd' in privilege).
Parliament, Occurrence, and Conscientious are all correctly spelt.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Privilege has NO 'd' (P-r-i-v-i-l-e-g-e).

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error:

Not only the divisional forest officer (A) / but also the field rangers (B) / was felicitated for their vigilance (C) / in checking timber poaching. (D)
options: Not only the divisional forest officer
questions.solution:
Correlative Conjunction Agreement: When subjects are connected by 'not only... but also', the verb agrees with the subject closer to it.
Here, the closer subject is 'the field rangers' (plural noun). Therefore, the finite verb must be plural: 'were felicitated' instead of 'was felicitated'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Not only A but also B -> Verb agrees with B (rangers = plural -> were).

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error:

The young botanist was confident to identify (A) / all endemic orchid species (B) / during the extensive survey (C) / across the Eastern Himalayas. (D)
options: The young botanist was confident to identify
questions.solution:
Prepositional Construction with 'Confident': The adjective 'confident' takes the preposition 'of' followed by a gerund (V-ing), rather than an infinitive ('to + V1').
Correct structure: '...was confident of identifying all endemic orchid species...'.
Segment (A) is grammatically incorrect.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Confident OF doing something (never 'confident to do').

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the option that improves the underlined part of the sentence. If no improvement is needed, select 'No improvement':

The endemic biodiversity of the Western Ghats <u>is far richer than the northern plains</u>.
options: is far richer than those of the northern plains
is far richer than that of the northern plains
is far richest than the northern plains
questions.solution:
Illogical Comparison Rule: A comparison must be made between parallel, corresponding entities. You cannot compare the 'biodiversity' (an abstract ecological quality) directly with 'the northern plains' (a geographic landform).
To maintain parallelism, use the demonstrative pronoun 'that of' to substitute for the singular noun 'biodiversity': 'is far richer than that of the northern plains'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Comparing attributes: The X of A is better than THAT OF B (never directly than B).

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence:

The wildlife protection task force had rescued thirty endangered sea turtles from illegal traffickers.
options: Thirty endangered sea turtles have been rescued from illegal traffickers by the wildlife protection task force.
Thirty endangered sea turtles had being rescued from illegal traffickers by the wildlife protection task force.
Thirty endangered sea turtles were rescued from illegal traffickers by the wildlife protection task force.
Thirty endangered sea turtles had been rescued from illegal traffickers by the wildlife protection task force.
questions.solution:
Past Perfect Active: Subject + had + V3 + Object.
Past Perfect Passive: Object + had + been + V3 (past participle) + by Subject.
'had rescued' -> 'had been rescued'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Active 'had + V3' -> Passive MUST have 'had been + V3'.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the correct indirect narration for the given sentence:

The senior forest warden said, "Alas! The last surviving great Indian bustard in the sanctuary has died."
options: The senior forest warden said alas that the last surviving great Indian bustard in the sanctuary had died.
The senior forest warden exclaimed sorrowfully that the last surviving great Indian bustard in the sanctuary had died.
The senior forest warden exclaimed with joy that the last surviving great Indian bustard in the sanctuary has died.
The senior forest warden told that alas the last surviving great Indian bustard in the sanctuary died.
questions.solution:
Indirect Narration of Exclamatory Sentences with 'Alas!':
1. Interjection 'Alas!' expresses grief or sorrow, so the reporting verb becomes 'exclaimed sorrowfully' or 'exclaimed with sorrow / grief'.
2. Conjunction 'that' connects the clause.
3. Present perfect ('has died') shifts to past perfect: 'had died'.
4. The interjection 'Alas!' is dropped.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: 'Alas!' -> exclaimed sorrowfully that... had + V3.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Select the most appropriate preposition to fill in the blank:

The tribal council steadfastly refused to yield ________ the relentless commercial pressures of the timber lobby.
questions.solution:
The intransitive verb 'yield' (meaning to give way to arguments, demands, or pressure; surrender) takes the fixed preposition 'to' (yield to pressure / yield to temptation).
Prepositions 'against', 'with', and 'for' are incorrect.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Fixed preposition: Yield TO pressure / authority (surrender to).

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph:

P. These designated wildlife corridors enable safe passage and gene flow among isolated tiger populations.
Q. The Western Ghats mountain range is home to some of the most biodiverse rainforests in South Asia.
R. However, expanding road networks and commercial plantations have severely severed historical animal migration paths.
S. In response to this fragmentation, conservation groups are collaborating with local villages to restore vegetative connectivity.
questions.solution:
Sentence Q introduces the habitat: 'The Western Ghats mountain range is home to biodiverse rainforests.'
Sentence R introduces the challenge with a contrast: 'However, expanding roads... have severely severed animal migration paths.'
Sentence S presents the conservation intervention: 'In response to this fragmentation, conservation groups are restoring vegetative connectivity.'
Sentence P describes the beneficial function of 'These designated wildlife corridors'.
Thus, the coherent sequence is Q-R-S-P.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Habitat intro (Q) -> Threat (R) -> Action response (S) -> Corridor benefit (P). Sequence = QRSP.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question:
Rearrange the given parts (P, Q, R, S) to form a grammatically correct and meaningful sentence:

(P) by integrating traditional ecological wisdom
(Q) long-term biodiversity preservation can be accomplished
(R) with rigorous modern conservation science
(S) in community-managed forest buffer reserves
questions.solution:
Step 1: Identify main subject and verb: Q ('Long-term biodiversity preservation can be accomplished...').
Step 2: Add prepositional phrase of location: S ('in community-managed forest buffer reserves...').
Step 3: Add manner/method clauses: P ('by integrating traditional ecological wisdom') coupled with R ('with rigorous modern conservation science').
The coherent sentence reads: 'Long-term biodiversity preservation can be accomplished (Q) in community-managed forest buffer reserves (S) by integrating traditional ecological wisdom (P) with rigorous modern conservation science (R).' Sequence = Q-S-P-R.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Main clause (Q) + Location (S) + Method (P + R) -> QSPR.

questions.subject: English Comprehension
questions.question: Read the excerpt from an environmental research paper and select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank: Mangrove ecosystems act as living breakwaters, blunting the destructive impact of cyclonic storm surges and protecting delicate shorelines from tidal erosion. Despite these indispensable ecological services, vast expanses of coastal mangroves have been ________ over recent decades to accommodate intensive commercial aquaculture ponds.
questions.solution:
The passage expresses strong contrast ('Despite these indispensable ecological services...') to show that vast tracts of coastal mangroves have been destroyed or drastically cut down to make way for shrimp farms.
'Decimated' means destroyed, drastically reduced, or killed in large numbers.
Proliferated, Augmented, and Fostered denote growth or encouragement, which contradict the destructive context.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Hook: Mangroves cleared and destroyed for aquaculture -> decimated.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Under which Article does the Supreme Court of India exercise exclusive Original Jurisdiction to adjudicate any legal dispute between the Government of India and one or more States?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Article 131

Explanation:

  • Article 131 of the Constitution gives the Supreme Court exclusive Original Jurisdiction in any dispute:
  • 1. Between the Government of India and one or more States.
  • 2. Between the Government of India and any State(s) on one side and one or more other States on the other.
  • 3. Between two or more States.
  • The dispute must involve any question of law or fact on which the existence or extent of a legal right depends.
  • Article 132–134 deal with Appellate Jurisdiction; Article 136 deals with Special Leave to Appeal (SLP); Article 143 deals with Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court upon presidential reference.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Article 131 = Centre vs State disputes (Exclusive Original Jurisdiction of Supreme Court).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 mandates what percentage of reservation in entry-level classes in private unaided schools for children from disadvantaged and economically weaker sections?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: 25%

Explanation:

  • The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009 came into force on 1 April 2010 to give operational effect to Fundamental Right Article 21A (inserted by the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002).
  • Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act mandates that all recognized private unaided schools must admit at least 25% of children in Class 1 (or pre-school entry level) from disadvantaged groups (SC, ST, OBC) and economically weaker sections (EWS) in the neighborhood, providing them completely free education, with tuition costs reimbursed by the State.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: RTE Sec 12(1)(c) = 25% quota for EWS/disadvantaged kids in private schools.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) regime in India, inserting Article 246A and Article 279A into the Constitution?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016

Explanation:

  • The 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016 paved the way for the historic roll-out of the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India on 1 July 2017.
  • Key constitutional changes:
  • - Article 246A: Conferred concurrent taxing powers upon both Parliament and State Legislatures to levy GST.
  • - Article 269A: Governs the levy and collection of Integrated GST (IGST) on inter-state supply of goods and services by the Centre, apportioned between Union and States.
  • - Article 279A: Mandated the creation of the GST Council, a joint constitutional forum chaired by the Union Finance Minister.
  • 100th Amendment dealt with the Land Boundary Agreement with Bangladesh; 102nd Amendment granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC); 103rd Amendment introduced 10% EWS reservation.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 101st CAA (2016) = GST Shagun (Articles 246A, 269A, 279A).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: India's three new criminal laws — the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) — officially came into force nationwide on which date?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: 1 July 2024

Explanation:

  • On 1 July 2024, India officially overhauled its colonial-era criminal justice framework as three new criminal laws came into full effect:
  • 1. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 - Replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.
  • 2. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 - Replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.
  • 3. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 - Replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
  • The laws received presidential assent in December 2023 and modernized criminal justice by introducing e-FIRs, zero FIR mandate, electronic evidence procedures, and community service as a penal punishment.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 1 July 2024 = Three New Criminal Laws (BNS, BNSS, BSA) in force!

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Under Article 360 of the Constitution of India, how many times has a Financial Emergency been declared in India since independence?
options: Once (during the 1991 Balance of Payments crisis)
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Never (Zero times)

Explanation:

  • Article 360 empowers the President to proclaim a Financial Emergency if he is satisfied that a situation has arisen whereby the financial stability or credit of India or any part of its territory is threatened.
  • A proclamation must be approved by both Houses of Parliament within 2 months. Once approved, it continues indefinitely until revoked by the President.
  • During a financial emergency, the President can order the reduction of salaries and allowances of all persons serving the Union, including the judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts.
  • A Financial Emergency has NEVER been declared in India to date (not even during the severe 1991 balance of payments crisis).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Article 360 = Financial Emergency = NEVER invoked in India (0 times).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The renowned Bronze Dancing Girl figurine and the Great Bath were unearthed from which famous Harappan archaeological site in the Larkana district of Sindh (Pakistan)?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Mohenjo-daro

Explanation:

  • Mohenjo-daro (meaning 'Mound of the Dead' in Sindhi) is located on the right bank of the Indus River in Larkana district, Sindh, Pakistan.
  • It was discovered and excavated by Rakhaldas Banerjee (R.D. Banerjee) in 1922.
  • Iconic archaeological finds at Mohenjo-daro include:
  • - The Great Bath (watertight brick tank lined with bitumen, used for ritual bathing).
  • - The Great Granary (largest building of Mohenjo-daro).
  • - Bronze statue of a Dancing Girl (crafted using the lost-wax / cire-perdue technique).
  • - Steatite sculpture of the 'Bearded Priest / King' and the Pashupati Seal.
  • Harappa was excavated by Daya Ram Sahni in 1921 on the Ravi River.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Mohenjo-daro (1922, RD Banerjee) = Great Bath + Bronze Dancing Girl + Bearded Priest.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate ruled for the longest period (from 1320 CE to 1414 CE)?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Tughlaq Dynasty

Explanation:

  • The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526 CE) witnessed the rule of five dynasties in chronological order:
  • 1. Mamluk / Slave Dynasty (1206–1290 CE): 84 years.
  • 2. Khalji Dynasty (1290–1320 CE): 30 years (shortest ruling dynasty).
  • 3. Tughlaq Dynasty (1320–1414 CE): 94 years (longest ruling dynasty), founded by Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq.
  • 4. Sayyid Dynasty (1414–1451 CE): 37 years.
  • 5. Lodi Dynasty (1451–1526 CE): 75 years (first Afghan dynasty in Delhi, ended by Babur at the 1st Battle of Panipat).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Chronology: S-K-T-S-L (Slave -> Khalji [Shortest 30y] -> Tughlaq [Longest 94y] -> Sayyid -> Lodi).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: During the balance-of-payments crisis of July 1991, the Reserve Bank of India carried out a two-step devaluation of the Indian Rupee on which two dates?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: 1 July and 3 July 1991

Explanation:

  • In mid-1991, India faced an unprecedented foreign exchange and balance of payments crisis with forex reserves barely sufficient for two weeks of imports.
  • Under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao and Finance Minister Dr. Manmohan Singh, the Reserve Bank of India undertook a coordinated two-step exchange rate adjustment:
  • - 1 July 1991: Rupee devalued by approximately 9%.
  • - 3 July 1991: Rupee devalued by a further 11%.
  • Cumulatively, the rupee depreciated by roughly 18.5% to 19% against major international currencies (US Dollar, Pound Sterling, Deutsche Mark, Yen) to arrest capital flight, spur exports, and restore external competitiveness.
  • This was followed by the landmark New Industrial Policy on 24 July 1991.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 1991 Crisis: Two-step Devaluation on 1 July (~9%) and 3 July (~11%).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: National Education Day is celebrated annually across India on 11 November to commemorate the birth anniversary of which great freedom fighter and independent India's first Minister of Education?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Maulana Abul Kalam Azad

Explanation:

  • National Education Day is celebrated every year on 11 November to commemorate the birth anniversary of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad (born 11 November 1888).
  • Maulana Azad was independent India's first Minister of Education (1947–1958) and was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 1992.
  • Under his stewardship, premier educational and cultural bodies were established:
  • - Indian Institute of Technology (IIT Kharagpur in 1951).
  • - University Grants Commission (UGC in 1953).
  • - Sahitya Akademi, Sangeet Natak Akademi, and Lalit Kala Akademi.
  • He was the youngest person to serve as Congress President (1923 special session) and led the INC from 1940 to 1946. Author of 'India Wins Freedom'.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Nov 11 = National Education Day = Maulana Abul Kalam Azad's birthday.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which strategic mountain pass across the Great Himalayan Range connects the Kashmir Valley (Srinagar) with Ladakh (Kargil and Leh)?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Zoji La Pass

Explanation:

  • Zoji La Pass is situated at an elevation of 3,528 metres (11,575 ft) on the Great Himalayas in the Union Territory of Ladakh, traversed by National Highway 1 (NH-1).
  • It connects Srinagar with Dras, Kargil, and Leh, serving as the primary lifeline between the Kashmir Valley and Ladakh.
  • (Asia's longest bi-directional all-weather road tunnel, the 14.15 km Zoji La Tunnel, is being constructed beneath it).
  • Shipki La connects Himachal Pradesh with Tibet (where River Sutlej enters India); Nathu La connects Sikkim with Tibet; Rohtang Pass connects Kullu Valley with Lahaul and Spiti.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Zoji La = Srinagar to Leh | Shipki La = Sutlej entry (HP to Tibet) | Nathu La = Sikkim to Tibet.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which port located on the Gulf of Kutch in Gujarat is India's largest private commercial port and the largest cargo-handling port by volume?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Mundra Port

Explanation:

  • Mundra Port, situated in the Kutch district of Gujarat on the northern shores of the Gulf of Kutch, is operated by Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ).
  • It is India's largest private commercial port and handles the highest cargo volume of any port in India (exceeding 170 million metric tonnes annually).
  • In contrast, Jawaharlal Nehru Port (JNPT / Nhava Sheva) in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, is India's largest public container-handling port (handling over 50% of India's container traffic).
  • Deendayal Port (Kandla) is a major public tidal port in Gujarat.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Mundra Port (Gujarat) = Largest private & highest total cargo port | JNPT = #1 Container port.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The historic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) for the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC) was signed on 9 September 2023 on the sidelines of which summit?
options: G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi

Explanation:

  • On 9 September 2023, during India's Presidency at the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, a landmark MoU was signed to establish the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC).
  • It comprises eight signatories: India, United States, Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates (UAE), France, Germany, Italy, and the European Union (EU).
  • IMEC consists of two distinct links:
  • 1. Eastern Corridor: Maritime connectivity from western Indian ports (Mundra, JNPT) to Arabian Gulf ports (Fujairah, Jebel Ali).
  • 2. Northern Corridor: Trans-continental rail and maritime link connecting the Arabian Gulf across Saudi Arabia and Jordan to Israel (Haifa port) and onwards to Europe (Piraeus, Greece).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: IMEC Corridor = Signed 9 Sep 2023 at G20 New Delhi (8 Signatories).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: In May 2024, India signed a landmark 10-year bilateral contract to operate the Shahid Beheshti terminal at Chabahar Port. In which country is Chabahar Port located?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Iran

Explanation:

  • Chabahar Port is located in the Sistan-Baluchestan province on the south-eastern coast of Iran along the Gulf of Oman.
  • On 13 May 2024, India Ports Global Limited (IPGL) and Iran's Ports and Maritime Organisation (PMO) signed a 10-year long-term agreement for the operation of the Shahid Beheshti terminal.
  • Strategic significance for India:
  • - Provides India a direct maritime trade corridor to landlocked Afghanistan, Central Asia, and Russia, completely bypassing Pakistan (and bypassing Gwadar Port in Balochistan).
  • - Acts as the southern gateway for the 7,200-km multi-modal International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Chabahar Port (Shahid Beheshti Terminal) = Iran (Gulf of Oman) -> Bypasses Pakistan.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: What is the policy interest rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) provides overnight liquidity to commercial banks against the collateral of government securities under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF)?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Repo Rate

Explanation:

  • Repo Rate (Repurchase Option Rate) is the benchmark interest rate at which the RBI lends short-term funds (overnight) to commercial banks against the collateral of eligible government securities under the Liquidity Adjustment Facility (LAF).
  • When the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) hikes the Repo Rate, borrowing costs for commercial banks rise, reducing credit creation and cooling inflation.
  • Reverse Repo Rate is the rate at which RBI absorbs surplus liquidity from banks.
  • In April 2022, RBI introduced the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) at 25 bps below the Repo Rate to absorb excess cash without providing collateral.
  • Bank Rate is the long-term lending rate without collateral under Section 49 of the RBI Act.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Repo Rate = RBI lends to Banks | Reverse Repo = RBI borrows from Banks.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY), launched in 2018 as the world's largest government-funded health assurance scheme, provides what health coverage per family per year?
options: Rs 2 lakh per family per year for primary and outpatient care
Rs 10 lakh per family per year for critical illness treatments only
Rs 3 lakh per family per year with a mandatory 20% co-payment
Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization

Explanation:

  • Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on 23 September 2018 from Ranchi, Jharkhand.
  • It provides a cashless and paperless health cover of Rs 5 lakh per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization across empanelled public and private hospitals.
  • Targeted initially at the bottom 40% of the population (covering over 12 crore poor and vulnerable families identified via SECC 2011).
  • In September 2024, the Union Cabinet expanded PM-JAY to provide free health insurance cover of Rs 5 lakh annually to all senior citizens aged 70 years and above, regardless of income.
  • It is implemented by the National Health Authority (NHA).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: PM-JAY (Ayushman Bharat) = Rs 5 Lakh/year/family for secondary & tertiary hospitalization.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: According to the World Happiness Report 2024 published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN), which country was ranked as the happiest nation in the world for the seventh consecutive year?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Finland

Explanation:

  • The World Happiness Report 2024 was published by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network (SDSN) in partnership with Gallup and the Oxford Wellbeing Research Centre.
  • Finland was ranked #1 in the world for the seventh consecutive year, followed by Denmark (#2), Iceland (#3), and Sweden (#4).
  • India was ranked 126th out of 143 surveyed nations (same rank as 2023).
  • Afghanistan was ranked at the very bottom (143rd) as the least happy nation.
  • Rankings are evaluated using Gallup World Poll life satisfaction data across 6 variables: GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perception of corruption.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: World Happiness 2024: Finland #1 (7th time) | India #126 | Afghanistan #143 (last).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: In the Union Budget, which of the following transactions is categorized under 'Revenue Expenditure' rather than Capital Expenditure?
options: Purchase of modern fighter aircraft and naval warships for defence
Payment of interest liabilities on national public debt
Disbursement of development loans to State Governments
Construction of four-lane national highways and expressways
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Payment of interest liabilities on national public debt

Explanation:

  • Expenditure in the Union Budget is divided into Revenue and Capital:
  • 1. Capital Expenditure: Results in the creation of physical/financial assets or reduction of liabilities. Examples: Construction of highways, railways, schools; capital acquisition of defence hardware; loans granted to states or foreign governments.
  • 2. Revenue Expenditure: Incurred for the routine, normal day-to-day functioning of government departments and administrative services. It neither creates any asset nor reduces any liability.
  • Examples of Revenue Expenditure: Interest payments on past borrowings (the single largest component of Union expenditure), subsidies, salaries and pensions of government staff, and grants-in-aid to States.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Interest payments = Revenue Expenditure (routine servicing, no asset created).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The transmission of optical signals through fiber-optic cables and the brilliant sparkling of a cut diamond are based on which optical phenomenon?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Total Internal Reflection (TIR)

Explanation:

  • Total Internal Reflection (TIR) occurs when a light ray travelling in an optically denser medium strikes the boundary of an optically rarer medium at an angle of incidence greater than the critical angle (c) for the two media.
  • When this happens, no refraction occurs; 100% of the incident light is reflected back into the denser medium.
  • Conditions for TIR:
  • 1. Light must travel from an optically denser medium to a rarer medium.
  • 2. Angle of incidence must exceed the critical angle (i > c).
  • Applications: Optical fibres (medical endoscopy, high-speed telecommunications), sparkling of diamonds (critical angle of diamond in air is very low, ~24.4°), mirage in deserts, and Porro prisms in binoculars.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Optical Fibres & Sparkling Diamonds = Total Internal Reflection (TIR) (Denser to rarer, i > c).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Plaster of Paris (PoP), commonly used for setting fractured bones and sculpting decorative casts, is chemically known as:
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Calcium Sulfate Hemihydrate (CaSO4·1/2H2O)

Explanation:

  • Plaster of Paris (PoP) is chemically Calcium Sulfate Hemihydrate: CaSO4·1/2H2O (or 2CaSO4·H2O).
  • It is prepared by heating Gypsum (Calcium Sulfate Dihydrate, CaSO4·2H2O) to a controlled temperature of 373 Kelvin (100 °C):
  • CaSO4·2H2O + Heat (373 K) -> CaSO4·1/2H2O + 1.5 H2O
  • When mixed with water, PoP re-hydrates back into gypsum, setting into a hard, rigid crystalline mass with a slight expansion in volume, making it ideal for medical casts and statues.
  • Bleaching powder is CaOCl2; Quicklime is CaO; Slaked lime is Ca(OH)2.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Gypsum = 2 H2O -> Heat to 373 K -> Plaster of Paris = 1/2 H2O.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: In the human kidney, the initial stage of urine formation—Ultrafiltration of blood under hydrostatic pressure—takes place in which micro-structure of the nephron?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Bowman's Capsule and Glomerulus (Malpighian Body)

Explanation:

  • The functional and structural microscopic unit of the kidney is the Nephron (approx. 1 million per kidney).
  • Urine formation involves three processes: Ultrafiltration, Selective Reabsorption, and Tubular Secretion.
  • Ultrafiltration takes place across the filtration membrane formed by the podocytes of Bowman's Capsule and the capillary endothelium of the Glomerulus (together called the Malpighian Body / Renal Corpuscle).
  • Blood pressure forces water, glucose, amino acids, salts, and urea through the microscopic pores into the capsular lumen (creating glomerular filtrate), while blood cells and large proteins are retained.
  • Loop of Henle concentrates urine; PCT reabsorbs 70–80% of electrolytes and water.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Ultrafiltration = Glomerulus + Bowman's Capsule (Malpighian Body).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: India's first dedicated space observatory to study the Sun, Aditya-L1, was successfully inserted by ISRO into a halo orbit around which Lagrange point on 6 January 2024?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Lagrange Point 1 (L1)

Explanation:

  • Aditya-L1 is India's first dedicated scientific space-based solar mission, launched by ISRO aboard PSLV-C57 on 2 September 2023 from Sriharikota.
  • On 6 January 2024, ISRO successfully inserted the spacecraft into a halo orbit around Sun-Earth Lagrange Point 1 (L1), situated approximately 1.5 million km from Earth (about 1% of the total Sun-Earth distance).
  • The L1 point provides an uninterrupted view of the Sun without eclipses or occultation.
  • The spacecraft carries seven scientific payloads, including the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) and Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT), to observe the solar photosphere, chromosphere, and corona.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Aditya-L1 = Sun Mission at Lagrange Point 1 (1.5 million km away) via PSLV-C57.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: India defeated South Africa by 7 runs in a thrilling final to win the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 at Bridgetown, Barbados. Who was adjudged the 'Player of the Tournament'?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Jasprit Bumrah

Explanation:

  • On 29 June 2024, India won the ICC Men's T20 World Cup 2024 by defeating South Africa by 7 runs at the Kensington Oval in Bridgetown, Barbados, under the captaincy of Rohit Sharma.
  • India ended an 11-year ICC trophy drought and became the first team to win the Men's T20 World Cup without losing a single match.
  • Key honours:
  • - Jasprit Bumrah was crowned Player of the Tournament for taking 15 wickets in 8 matches at an extraordinary economy rate of 4.17.
  • - Virat Kohli was named Player of the Match in the Final for his match-winning knock of 76 runs off 59 balls.
  • - Arshdeep Singh (India) and Fazalhaq Farooqi (Afghanistan) were the joint-highest wicket-takers with 17 wickets each.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: T20 World Cup 2024: Player of Tournament = Bumrah | Player of Final = Kohli (76) | Capt = Rohit.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: On 15 November 2023 at the Wankhede Stadium in Mumbai, who broke Sachin Tendulkar's legendary world record of 49 ODI centuries by scoring his 50th One Day International hundred?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Virat Kohli

Explanation:

  • On 15 November 2023, during the ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2023 semifinal against New Zealand at Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, Virat Kohli scored his 50th ODI century (117 off 113 balls).
  • He officially broke Sachin Tendulkar's record of 49 ODI centuries in front of Tendulkar himself in the stadium.
  • Kohli achieved his 50th ODI century in just 279 innings, whereas Tendulkar had taken 452 innings to reach 49 centuries.
  • Kohli also scored 765 runs in the 2023 tournament, the highest ever by a batsman in a single edition of the Cricket World Cup.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: Virat Kohli = 50th ODI Century at Wankhede Stadium vs NZ (15 Nov 2023).

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: At the 24th Meeting of the Council of Heads of State of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) held in Astana in July 2024, which country was admitted as the 10th full member state?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Belarus

Explanation:

  • The 24th SCO Summit was held on 3–4 July 2024 in Astana, Kazakhstan.
  • During this summit, Belarus was officially inducted as the 10th full member state of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO).
  • Members of SCO (10 nations): China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, India (joined 2017), Pakistan (joined 2017), Iran (joined 2023), and Belarus (joined 2024).
  • Headquarters of SCO: Beijing, China; Regional Anti-Terrorist Structure (RATS) is based in Tashkent, Uzbekistan.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 10th SCO Member (Astana 2024) = BELARUS.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas', inscribed in September 2023 as India's 42nd UNESCO World Heritage Site, consists of stellar temples in Belur, Halebidu, and Somanathapura in Karnataka built using which stone?
questions.solution:
Correct Answer: Chloritic Schist (Soapstone)

Explanation:

  • In September 2023, the 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas' in Karnataka was inscribed as India's 42nd UNESCO World Heritage Site (at the 45th World Heritage Committee session in Riyadh).
  • The site comprises three exquisite 12th–13th century temples:
  • 1. Chennakeshava Temple at Belur (commissioned by King Vishnuvardhana).
  • 2. Hoysaleswara Temple at Halebidu (Dwarasamudra).
  • 3. Keshava Temple at Somanathapura (built under King Narasimha III).
  • Hoysala architecture is famed for its stellate (star-shaped) ground plans, jagati platforms, and intricate microscopic carvings made from soft Chloritic Schist (Soapstone), which hardens upon exposure to air.
  • (Santiniketan in West Bengal was inscribed as India's 41st site at the same session).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Memory Hook: 42nd UNESCO Site = Hoysala Temples (Belur, Halebidu, Somanathapura) carved from Soapstone.
